instructions: Pat the steak dry and cut it into 1-inch cubes. Transfer them to a bowl and toss with the salt, pepper and rosemary. Mince the garlic.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Add the oil.
Add half the steak in a single layer, with space between the pieces. Leave it alone for 2 minutes, until the underside is deep brown. Stir and cook for 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

You're cooking the steak to 135°F in the middle for medium rare, and it rises a few degrees as it sits. If you have a thermometer, check a piece there. No thermometer? Cut one in half: it should be pink in the middle.
Cook the rest of the steak the same way and transfer it to the plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until the garlic smells good. Don't let it brown.
Return the steak and any juices from the plate to the pan. Toss for 30 seconds to coat it in the butter, then take the pan off the heat.
Chop 1 tbsp of the parsley and scatter it over the top. Serve with mashed potatoes and green beans.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Both sources sear cubed sirloin hot in a single layer, then add the butter and garlic over lower heat and toss the steak back in. Spend with Pennies seasons with rosemary and finishes with 2 tbsp butter; Crayons and Cravings uses Italian seasoning and cooks diced onion in 4 tbsp butter. This follows the lead, with a little more butter (3 tbsp) and garlic for a proper garlic butter sauce, and the steak is cooked in two batches so it browns. About 22 minutes in all.
